_note: General investigation guidance per finding type. Shown as 'General guidance, not derived from your data'. One to three steps, each under 20 words.
SQL Injection: Check the response size of the flagged requests for unusually large replies.
Review database logs for queries at the same time.
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): Check whether the input is stored and shown to other users.
Confirm output encoding on the affected page.
Path Traversal / LFI: Compare response sizes with normal requests to the same path.
Verify the server cannot read files outside the web root.
Command Injection: Look for new processes started by the web server account.
Check for outbound connections from the web server.
Web Shell / Sensitive File Probe: Confirm the probed files are not reachable from the internet.
Search the web root for recently changed script files.
Scanner / Attack-Tool User-Agent: Look for follow-up requests from the same source after the scan.
Directory / Vulnerability Scanning: List which scanned paths returned success codes.
SSH / Login Brute Force: List every account the source tried and reset weak passwords.
Check whether key-based authentication can replace passwords.
Successful Login After Failures: Review the session that followed the successful login.
Check shell history and new files for that account.
PowerShell Encoded Command: Decode the full command and record every URL or file it touches.
Check the endpoint for the downloaded script.
PowerShell Download Cradle: Block the download URL and search proxy logs for other hosts fetching it.
PowerShell Execution Policy Bypass: Find the parent process that launched PowerShell.
PowerShell Hidden Window / No Profile: Check which user account ran the hidden PowerShell session.
TCP Port Scan Detected: Check whether the scan source later connected to any open port.
Cleartext Credentials on the Wire: Rotate the exposed credentials and check where else they are used.
Traffic to Suspicious Port: Identify the process that opened the connection on the source host.
Risky Port Open: Confirm each exposed service is required and restrict access to it.
Vulnerable Service: Confirm the real installed version; banners can be outdated or backported.
NSE Finding: Re-run the Nmap script after patching to confirm the fix.
End-of-Life Operating System: Plan an upgrade or isolate the host from untrusted networks.
SPF Authentication Failed: Check whether other messages from this sender reached users.
DMARC Authentication Failed: Search mail logs for other messages claiming the same domain.
Link Text / Destination Mismatch: Check proxy logs for clicks on the real destination.
Double-Extension Attachment: Search mailboxes for the same attachment hash.
Reply-To Hijack: Check whether anyone replied to the hijacked address.
Shortened URL: Expand the short link in a sandbox before anyone visits it.
Newly Registered Domain: Watch for other lookalike domains registered at the same time.
default: Corroborate the finding with a second data source before acting on it.
